heading: Focus in dialogs and menus
body:
A dialog, a menu or a drawer must move keyboard focus. When it opens, focus goes inside it. While it is open, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it. When it closes, focus goes back to the button that opened it. The `Focus` browser API does these three steps for a Tac service (ADR 0115).

| Language | How the service gets it | Calls | A failure at once |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript, TypeScript | `@Needs focus` (type `Focus`) | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | an error is thrown |
| Rust | a field `focus: Focus`, which `Default` fills | `move_to(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | an `Err` value |
| Go | `// @Needs` above a `focus Focus` field | `Move(target)`, `Trap(container)`, `Release()` | an `error` value |
| C# | `private readonly Focus focus = new();` | `Move(target)`, `Trap(container)`, `Release()` | an `InvalidOperationException` |
| F# | `let focus = Focus()` in the type | `Move(target)`, `Trap(container)`, `Release()` | an `InvalidOperationException` |
| Swift | `private let focus = Focus()` | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | an error is thrown; call with `try` |
| Kotlin | `private val focus = Focus()` | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | an `IllegalStateException` |
| Java | `private final Focus focus = new Focus();` | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | an `IllegalStateException` |
| Dart | `@Needs()` above `final Focus focus;` | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | a `StateError` |
| Ruby | `Focus.new` | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release` | a `RuntimeError` |
| Lua | the table `Focus`, called with `:` | `Focus:move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | a Lua error; catch it with `pcall` |
| C++ | `[[Needs]] Focus& focus;` | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | a `std::runtime_error` is thrown |
| Python | a field `focus: Annotated[Focus, needs]` | `move(target)`, `trap(container)`, `release()` | a `RuntimeError` |

Name each element with `data-focus="name"` in the view. A name is a letter, then up to 63 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. A service reaches only the elements that its own components show.

- `Trap(container)` focuses the first element inside the container that Tab can reach, and keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it. If the container has no such element, the container itself takes focus, so give it `tabindex="-1"`.
- `Move(target)` focuses one element. An element that passes focus to a child, such as a custom element with a shadow root that uses `delegatesFocus`, counts as focused when focus lands inside it.
- `Release()` ends the service's latest trap and focuses the element that had focus when `Trap` was called.

Each call waits for the next render, so the dialog can open in the same method. Calls run in the order they were made. A wrong name, or a service that no shown component uses, fails at once. A failure after the render (no element has the name, two elements have it, or the element cannot take focus) arrives as a `BrowserCallFailed` event with `api` set to `focus`. The API needs no permission, so the manifest grants nothing for it. It works the same in a browser tab and in the macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android apps, because the page runs in the browser or in the platform web view. In a Go test unit, answer a call with `BrowserFakes{}.Answer("focus", "move", nil)`.

Rust's call is `move_to`, because `move` is a Rust keyword. In a test unit, give each call an answer with the language's browser fakes, as for the other browser APIs (see "Browser APIs in test units"). A service that is linked into a native app has no page, so the build refuses `Focus` in it (`TY1317`).
